newsitem.title: USA: CVRD sale seen important for Brazil.
newsitem.headline: CVRD sale seen important for Brazil.

text.p: The sale of Brazilian mining giant Companhia Vale do Rio Doce (CVRD) is important for foreign investors' confidence in Brazil's economy, analysts and traders said Tuesday.

They said Tuesday's scheduled auction, delayed by a swarm of lawsuits from opponents of the sale, would set the stage for multibillion dollar sales of state-run utilities and telephone companies. They are likely to start late this year or in 1998.

"It's going to be very important because it's the first of the blue chips to be privatized and because being sold will boost the confidence of investors in privatization," said Alvaro Maia, head of equity sales for Caspian Securities in Brazil.

Eveline Freire Gerck, an analyst at Daiwa Securities America Inc, said: "If this auction doesn't happen and they continue to do all these injunctions, the government and the country and even the stock market are going to lose a lot of credibilty."
Brazil's reformist government has battled for years to sell off CVRD, the world's largest iron ore exporter and the crown jewel of state-run companies.

The auction of 45 percent of the voting shares at the Rio de Janeiro stock exchange is expected to raise about $2.8 billion. Once completed, the sale will raise about $5 billion, the biggest privatization in Latin American history.

Two consortiums were expected to bid on Tuesday. One is led by Brazilian steelmaker Companhia Siderurgica Nacional and the other by Brazilian conglomerate Votorantim Inc and mining firm Anglo American Corp of South Africa.
Gerck said the Votorantim group was likely to win the bidding, calling it in a report "the government and CVRD's management's dream team."

Tuesday's sale was delayed by lawsuits from opponents of the privatisation. Maia said that, if the auction was not done Tuesday it might be held Wednesday or next week, since Thursday is the May Day national holiday.
"In Brazil there is always something at the last minute," a trader said. "This is going to be big news when it happens."
